segments.line: In nineteen seventy, the state of Oregon blew up a whale. On purpose. With
half a ton of dynamite. And buddy, this ain't some tall tale. It's on film. Here's the deal.
November, a little beach town called Florence. A
forty- five foot sperm whale washes up dead. Eight tons. And it stinks to high heaven.
Now, in Oregon, the beach counted as a highway. So the whale was the highway department's problem.
Their plan? Blow it into tiny pieces and let the seagulls clean up. What could go wrong?
One fella in the crowd, an old army explosives man, said that's way too much dynamite. Nobody listened.
Twenty cases of dynamite. The countdown. And...
KABOOM. Sand, smoke, and then it
rained whale. Chunks of blubber came down on the crowd like the sky had a bellyache.
One chunk flattened a brand- new car. And whose car was it? The army man's. The
way he told it, he bought it at a sale called Get a Whale of a Deal. And the
seagulls? Scared off by the boom. Didn't touch a bite.
Most of the whale was still lying right there. So they buried it. Like they should've done in the first place.
Today, Florence has a park called Exploding Whale Memorial Park. That's real. So
next time somebody says I've got a plan, ask how much dynamite.
That's about it, folks. Follow for more strange history. See ya!
